commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Preserve GSM8K answers without crediting operands (#10808)

Port the GSM8K extraction and scoring rules from Evalchemy commit
a993b52543c493e58956be94ed6d3420b94143c0 into Marin's vendored
evaluator. These rules were used for the corrected 2026 September
evaluation campaign associated with #10197 but were absent from current
main.

Flexible extraction passes the complete final boxed text to the scorer,
preserving 11:30, currency and nested LaTeX. Restore acceptance of unit
annotations and arithmetic forms, such as $139 for 139 and 3 onions + 1
potato for 4. For questions containing "time", accept whole-hour clock
answers such as 2:00 for 2. For questions containing "percent" or "pass
rate", accept a fractional form such as 1/4 for 25. An incorrect final
box must not receive credit from an earlier number in the reasoning.

Unlike the historical patch, scalar fallbacks match complete scalar or
annotated answers. They do not credit an operand from 1/4, 3 + 1 or
11:30, or the radicand of sqrt(4). Regression tests cover those false
positives and preserve correct full-expression grading.

Replaying stored responses can change exact_match. The diff changes only
the GSM8K task scorer, its regression tests and runtime notes; metric
names, prompts and generation settings remain unchanged. NUPA and the
Mini/Micro subset machinery are outside this change.

RNO2A CPU validation passed all 102 selected GSM8K and shared-math
grader checks, including the generated-answer extraction path. The
repository pre-commit entry point passed and the advisory review
reported no findings.

commits.message:
Patch dependency vulnerabilities across Python, npm, and Rust (#10803)

Require patched dependencies in the root and Grafana Python
environments, nine frontend lockfiles, and three Rust workspaces.
Rebuild the shipped inference dashboard with DOMPurify 3.4.17 and Vue
3.5.44. Remove Black from Marin's lint dependency group; the required
lint command already runs its own isolated formatter through uvx.

Move Datasets to 5.0.1 and fsspec/gcsfs/s3fs to 2026.6.0 together
because the previous Datasets cap excluded the patched storage versions.
Refresh dependent local-package lock metadata. Move S3 cache directories
through explicit file pairs so stricter copy-error handling skips
synthetic prefixes and still rejects missing real objects.

Upgrade Finelog's buffa, buffa-types, and ConnectRPC runtime/code
generator to the 0.8 family. Replace the affected OwnedView request
interfaces with borrowed ServiceRequest handlers and retain shared Arrow
IPC bytes across blocking storage calls. Preserve InvalidArgument
responses for malformed zstd requests through both decoder paths.

Enable grouped Dependabot security updates for all tracked uv projects,
npm projects, and Cargo workspaces while keeping routine version-update
PRs disabled.

Seven reviewed alerts remain unresolved: Torch needs a coordinated
CUDA/Triton upgrade, Thrift requires a query-engine migration, and
Grafana's moment/React Router dependencies require matching host/SDK
changes. Accelerate and deepmerge still lack verified upstream fixes.

The native dependency fixes require rebuilding and adopting the affected
wheels or images before existing deployments benefit.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Move SOTOPIA scoring into Harbor and count repeated trials (#10670)

Compute SOTOPIA length-controlled scores in Harbor at job completion.
Length is the evaluated agent's emitted character count. Report the
corrected overall score as the continuous primary metric, preserve raw
rewards, and have Marin read Harbor's result without recomputing the
correction.

Require an explicit comparison cohort in the Harbor job configuration.
The `eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled` configs supply a versioned 13-model
baseline cohort. Match the candidate's original model location to the
cohort, replacing its baseline entry with the current run or adding it
if absent. Save the source archive locations, hashes of the cohort and
fit inputs, fitted correction, and adjusted episode scores under
`metric_evidence` in Harbor's `result.json`. Resolve completed trial
summaries against the current job directory when resuming a relocated
job. Missing baseline archives or transcript summaries for scored
episodes fail the Harbor job and record the run as `failed`.

Preserve the original model location in Harbor's `model_name` and route
requests using its existing `model_alias` field. This keeps model
provenance and trial resume identity stable when a serving alias
changes. SOTOPIA and AIME route inference through the alias, and ACP
uses it for session selection.

Remove the Marin SOTOPIA wrapper and its fitting dependency extra. The
campaign's `analysis/sotopia_length_control/rank.py` reuses Harbor's
calculation and runs in Harbor's environment. Changing the campaign
cohort invalidates SOTOPIA's cache identity while preserving
FinanceBench and OlympiadBench identities.

Count independently sampled Evalchemy repetitions as separate coverage
items, counting each trial only once across extraction filters. Use
declared trial counts to retain missing repetitions in the coverage
denominator and replace the OlympiadBench-specific counting workaround.

Part of #10197.

commits.message:
[datakit] Register CalibForge relay SFT traces as chat (#10027)

Register the `terminus2_relay_sft` configuration of [laion/calibforge-relay-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/laion/calibforge-relay-traces), pinned at `66feab4`, as `calibforge-relay/terminus2` in Datakit's chat registry. The source combines CalibForge student/teacher relay episodes and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces for decontamination and downstream harness conversion.

Parse each reply once through the shared Terminus parser. CalibForge enables supported JSON-closing repairs and joins closed reasoning spans; the existing Terminus adapters use strict parsing. Drop an episode if any assistant reply lacks a command, including student replies excluded from the source training loss, and reject unfinished reasoning so its example commands cannot become actions. Commands remain JSON text in assistant messages; conversion to mini SWE agent actions is downstream work.

Preserve teacher, task source, outcome, and `source_train_turns` metadata. The `source_train_turns` flags describe source messages after removing the template-only system message. Reasoning and final text may become separate output messages, and the renderer and trainer do not apply these flags as a loss mask. Training on rendered text therefore also supervises student turns and does not reproduce the original teacher-only training recipe.

[datakit] Restore missing HF files on download reruns (#10778)

`download_hf` now checks each destination before fetching its Hugging
Face file. Missing or size-mismatched files are streamed, and complete
files are reused. Zephyr rewrites its metrics shards on rerun so an

A rerun previously returned successfully after a destination was deleted

truncated destinations. In a 128-file local fixture, one deleted file
was restored; the other 127 were reused before any source read. Those
reused files totaled 16.6 MiB. Reuse compares file sizes, so callers
should pin the source revision when writing repeatedly to one output
path.

Fixes #10766

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
[grug] Clip the hero gradient norm at 1.0 and prepare its handoff (#10783)

Clip the hero's total gradient norm to 1.0 in the train step, and
prepare the handoff to the clipped run `hero-gradclip-step<N>k`. The
running `hero-ctx16k-step257k` is unaffected until it is relaunched from
this commit. Merge only after N is filled in at cutover.

#10677 traced the hero's gradient spikes to single 16K sequences. They
are long, repetitive, sink-less windows. At the exact bf16 forward
state, their per-sequence gradient is enormous, and it compounds from
the upper layers down to the embeddings. Since step 340000 the median
`grad/norm/total` is 0.501.

Step 352190 reached 4.49. Step 353060 reached 20.84 (41.6x the median):
- Layers 0–26 were 50–208x their recent medians, with the peak at layer
22. Layers 29–47 were 1.3–2.3x.
- `token_embed` was 138x.
- The loss jumped from 1.018 at step 353060 to 1.101 at step 353061, the
only rise above 0.05 since step 351000.
- It recovered over about 50 steps. The mean loss was 1.018 over
353040–353059, 1.073 over 353061–353065, 1.030 over 353076–353085, and
1.018 over 353101–353140.

The norm is logged only every 10th step, so spikes on the other nine
steps are never seen.

The train step now computes `optax.global_norm` over the whole gradient,
the quantity W&B logs as `grad/norm/total`. Above `max_grad_norm`, it
scales every leaf by `max_norm / norm` before the optimizer. At or below
the limit, every leaf is multiplied by exactly 1.
- Every step logs `train/grad_norm` (pre-clip) and `train/grad_clipped`.
The watch's `grad/norm/*` keep their pre-clip meaning and their 10-step
cadence.
- `HERO_MAX_GRAD_NORM = 1.0` is required by `hero_grug_trainer_config`
and set for the d6144 rung. The narrow ladder rungs stay unclipped.
- `launch_diagnostics --max-grad-norm` defaults to 1.0.

The clip is outside the optimizer, so the opt_state pytree and
checkpoint layout do not change, and current hero checkpoints restore as
they are. The optimizer's existing per-group `max_grad_norm` would not:
it prepends `clip_by_global_norm` to each muonh/adamh/adam chain. That
moves every opt_state key, for example from
`inner_states['adam'].inner_state[0].mu` to `.inner_state[1].mu`
(checked with `jax.eval_shape`). It also clips each group on its own
norm rather than the total. That path is left unused.

`current_run.py` and `trigger_hero.sh` follow the #9960 and #10101
handoffs, with N left as `REPLACE_BEFORE_DEPLOYMENT`. The script refuses
to fork or launch with that value. The three values are:
- `hero-gradclip-step<N/1000>k`;
-
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx16k-step257k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-N`;
- `hero-ctx16k-step257k?_step=<N-1>`.

The cutover follows the README's "Hero cutovers and W&B lineage" and
`code-cutover.md`:
1. Request a permanent checkpoint from the old run's training-control
endpoint, with header `X-Levanter-Training-Control:
request-permanent-checkpoint`. The hero's code at `eadf76a1bc` wires
`TrainingDashboard` to `Checkpointer.request_checkpoint`. That maps the
request to PERMANENT retention, and the next step saves `step-N` to the
permanent root with `is_temporary: false`.
2. Wait for that `metadata.json` with `"is_temporary": false`, and
confirm on the parent that `_step` N−1 is `global_step` N−1. It was at
353999.
3. Fill in N and merge.
4. Let the old run record the 200-step matched control window after
`step-N` before stopping it.
5. Run `trigger_hero.sh fork-wandb`, stop the old coordinator, then run
`trigger_hero.sh launch`.
6. Apply the agreed gates. Rollback relaunches `hero-ctx16k-step257k` at
`eadf76a1bc`.

Two one-rack resume tests restored the hero's permanent `step-354000`
read-only on cw-us-east-08a at production priority. Settings:
- global batch 256 (2816 / 11);
- the hero's optimizer sized for batch 2816 (beta2 0.95, epsilon
6.04e-15), with MuonH and Adam learning rates × sqrt(1/11) (0.000992 and
0.000229);
- clip 1.0;
- output under
`s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=30d/hero-clip-resume-test/`.

rt1 ran `f00d75cff3`, and rt2 ran `0d56a910a5`. Both set the batch-2816
sizing and the LR scale with temporary diagnostic flags
(`--optimizer-batch-size 2816 --lr-scale 0.3015`). The flags are not
part of this PR; branch state `2f7e57ae26` has them. The clip and the
train step are unchanged since those runs.

| |
[hero-clip-rt1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-clip-rt1)
|
[hero-clip-rt2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-clip-rt2)
|
| --- | --- | --- |
| steps | 354000–354032, cancelled | 354000–354019 |
| loss at 354000 | 1.014783 (hero 1.022036 on its full batch) | 1.014783
|
| mean loss 354001–354019 | 1.023 (hero 1.017) | 1.023, within 1.2e-4 of
rt1 per step |
| median `train/grad_norm` | 0.39, logged every step | 0.39, logged
every step |
| clip fired | 354012 (1.041), 354029 (1.975) | 354002 (3.228) |
| step time, MFU | 13.4 s, 31.5% (hero 13.7–18.0 s) | 13.2 s, 31.8% |
| peak memory | 123.21 GiB | 123.21 GiB |

Results:
- No step produced a NaN.
- `train/grad_clipped` equals `train/grad_norm > 1` on every row.
- `train/grad_norm` equals the watch's `grad/norm/total` on every 10th
step.
- rt1's first attempt lost two ranks to a tokenizer-staging race in
`/tmp/levanter_tokenizers` after a clean 188 s restore; its automatic
retry trained.

The two runs see identical batches from identical weights, yet their
spikes land on different steps. This matches #10677's finding that a
spike sits at an ill-conditioned point that rounding moves. The fire
rate at batch 256 does not predict the hero's: one pathological sequence
carries 11x more weight in a 256-row mean. At the hero's median of 0.50,
the clip should fire on spikes like 352190 and 353060.

New CPU tests cover:
- the clip's bitwise no-op and its global rescale;
- the clipped train step;
- restoring an unclipped checkpoint into a clipping run.

The `tests/test_moe_hero_ep.py`, `test_scaling_ladder.py`, and
`test_grug_variant_contracts.py` suites pass (110 tests), and
`./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files` is clean. `--review` flagged three
issues:
- a positional tuple return, now the `ClippedGradients` NamedTuple;
- rollout context in the clip constant's comment, now removed;
- a bare `"d6144"` literal, left as is because the file already compares
against it in several places.

Part of #10677.

commits.author: GBX-Max1220
commits.message:
Screening findings for same-history preference pairs from agent traces (Marin #10042) (#10741)

## Screening findings for same-history preference pairs (Marin #10042)

Adds a feasibility screening artifact for the "local DPO from agent
traces" question, plus the code that reproduces it. It does **not**
construct preference pairs and does not train anything.

**What it establishes**

- **Parser-tier screening is feasible on this data.** Exact prompt token
ids, a served tool schema extracted per-turn from each completion prefix
(not a single first-prompt pull), and provable action spans for 123 of
156 completion turns. Within every one of the 22 rows the schema is
byte-identical across that row's per-turn prefixes (22/22 rows, one
schema hash per row); cross-row identity was not separately verified.
The span proof has three gates reported separately: round trip
(`encode(decode(ids)) == ids`), exactly one `<function=...>` block, and
a three-way segmentation check that fails when a single token spans an
action boundary.
- **Natural preference pairs are not established.** The sample holds one
trace per task id, so there is no second branch under the same history
to compare; there is also no per-action outcome label and no pre-action
environment state.

**Findings**

1. **Pairing evidence.** Provided: `instruction` / prompt ids / action
ids / completion logprobs 22/22, served schema extracted 22/22 --
extraction only; agreement with what the engine actually served is
**not** verified (the export carries no independent record to compare
against). Missing: execution-result column, pre-action environment-state
column, per-step verifier (the verifier is episode-level).
`conversations` carries no `tool` role in this export, but 133 of 156
assistant turns are followed by a non-empty message with tool-result
characteristics. Those are called *following messages*, not
observations: the data does not establish that they came from the
environment in response to the call, and they are unlabeled and
unframed. The gap is structure, not text.
2. **Natural format phenomena (156 turns).** 91 clean-parsable; 32 over
an operator-set 512-token cap (proven spans -- length, not format); 22
prose turns (**not** tool calls, so not malformed); 8
multiple-function-block turns (a **multiple-block phenomenon; harness
validity not fully established** -- the opencode adapter's `findall`
over the `conversations`-column `<tool_call>` envelopes shows the
exported format supports multiple calls per message, but it does not
operate on the native literal token stream, so native multi-block
validity is unverified); 3 tokenizer round-trip artifacts. Zero turns
are established as natural malformed calls, which is absence of
confirmed positives under one narrow parser, not evidence the data is
clean.
3. **Recorded on-policy logprobs.** Completion side only, one scalar per
token (not top-k). Low-probability tokens (`< -1.0`, threshold fixed a
priori) are less frequent inside action spans (656 / 42,648 = 1.538%)
than in the surrounding text of the same turns (260 / 5,384 = 4.829%).
The correspondence check is **token-count agreement only** (156/156
turns, 0 mismatches) -- positional correspondence is assumed, not
verified. These are the generating model's own confidence, not a
disagreement signal, so low probability is not used as an error label.

**Next steps (detailed in the README)**

1. Reconcile the adapter's one-observation-per-call rule with this
export -- it currently rejects rows for a reason unrelated to model
behaviour.
2. Get a slice with >= 2 attempts per task id, or per-step environment
results instead of the episode-level verifier. This is a screening
condition, not permission to pair: prefixes must be equal token by
token, schema identical at both decision points, pre-action environment
state verifiably equivalent, and the contrast must fall on the action
rather than the episode outcome.
3. Only then derive a real error taxonomy from harness-side parse
failures, and use it to judge any synthetic corruption distribution.

**Limits**

- Snowball rescoring was **not** executed: the stored Qwen ids cannot be
reused directly as Snowball input (vocabulary mismatch), and the
text-level route was not attempted, not verified, and not costed.
- One cohort, one harness, one native serialization; n = 156 turns. The
512-token cap is operator-set, not a data property.
- The source dataset declares no license, so only aggregate counts are
printed, never raw record text.
- The synthetic corruption rule is deliberately out of scope.
- When a per-turn prefix carries no `<tools>` block, the schema is
reported as schema-unavailable and that turn is counted separately -- it
is never auto-classified as malformed.

**Files** -- `experiments/post_training/trace_preferences/`: `README.md`
(findings + reproduction), `parse.py`, `analyze_traces.py`,
`test_trace_prefs.py`. 614 lines of Python across 3 files (the count
includes the tests); this is above Ben's suggested ~500-line budget --
the excess is entirely the per-turn schema extraction, the
confirmed/undetermined malformed separation, and the targeted tests
added during review. The tests live beside the experiment per
`experiments/AGENTS.md`.

CPU only, no model run, no API calls, nothing downloaded. The sample and
tokenizer are not in the repo: paths are passed explicitly and the
real-data test skips when they are absent, so it never fails on a fresh
checkout.


Related to issue #10042.

---------

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <bf996@nyu.edu>

Raise patched Python dependency floors across locked environments (#10748)

Require Authlib >=1.9.1, dnspython >=2.9.0, GitPython >=3.2.0, msgpack
>=1.2.3 and NLTK >=3.10.4 in the affected environments. Refresh the
root, SkyRL, Harbor, Evalchemy and OlympiadBench ablation locks
independently. Only the affected package versions change; Evalchemy
keeps GitPython 3.2.1. [OAuthLib 4 is a separate
change](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10749) because its
release changes grant validation and removes JSONP support.

These floors address the reviewed advisories for [Authlib JWS
validation](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6v38-4h7w-rj9h), [empty
HMAC keys](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8m4g-j4wp-wgcg), [key
confusion](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7vr2-2fgp-9w7p),
[dnspython](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-45c3-73f7-pv4m),
[GitPython command
wrappers](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w8jc-g24h-crhw), [GitPython
metadata parsing](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m64x-33q8-m5h7),
[msgpack](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j586-36cw-2gc2) and
[NLTK](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j456-xh4h-cpf2). Affected lock
entries establish dependency exposure; no exploitation is claimed.

All five locks pass offline freshness checks. Required diff-scoped lint
and branch advisory review complete with no findings. Harbor's offline
runtime passes 987 tests and all 3 acquisition tests pass. Positive
compatibility probes pass for signed JWTs and mocked OAuth clients,
repository metadata and boolean config, in-memory DNS wire parsing,
msgpack and Flax checkpoint roundtrips, and NLTK corpus, sentence,
ROUGE, IFBench and IFEval paths. NLTK resources reside in a private data
directory; resource-path confinement remains enabled. No live
credentials or exploit reproductions are used; accelerator runtime
behavior remains untested locally.

The macOS root suite reports 3,064 passed, 11 skipped and 5 expected
failures, with one Linux-only bubblewrap failure and four collection
errors from missing optional Torch; all five issues reproduce on
unchanged main 755a737. Evalchemy reports 827 passed, 22 skipped and 21
failures in sandbox resource-limit/multiprocessing checks and a
temporary-path assertion. Representative failures from all three
categories reproduce on main. Its 17 NLTK sentence-grader tests and
Levanter's GitPython integration test pass. Linux CI passes at
300303074b, including Evalchemy, SkyRL, Harbor and the Levanter
Torch/TPU lanes. The affected-test runner's broad command omits the test
group, so the root suite was run with `uv run --frozen --package
marin-core --group test pytest -n 2`, preserving default safety markers.

[iac] Declare an existing Marin Dev grant in Pulumi (#10781)

Grant `projects/hai-gcp-models/roles/marindev` on `hai-gcp-models` to
one KMS-encrypted human principal (`human-085`). The live project policy
already has this member, but `iam_data.yaml` does not. The role's
`IAMBinding` owns the full member set, so the next `pulumi up` would
remove the member.

A grant approver should run `review-grant` to confirm the decrypted
principal, then merge and run `pulumi up` on the `marin` stack.

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

[iac] Grant Marin Dev access to two developers (#10775)

Grant `projects/hai-gcp-models/roles/marindev` on `hai-gcp-models` to
two KMS-encrypted human principals for standard Marin development and
TPU work. The existing `domain:stanford.edu` members on the
`iris-marin-be` and `iris-marin-dev-be` IAP bindings already cover both
accounts.

A grant approver should run `review-grant` to confirm the decrypted
identities and role, then merge and run `pulumi up` on the `marin` stack
in `infra/pulumi`.
